entries.claim: On a number line, one real number $a$ corresponds to point P; $a$ is called the coordinate of P, and P with coordinate $a$ is denoted P($a$).
entries.quote: On a number line, one real number a corresponds to point P.

entries.claim: The distance AB between A($a$) and B($b$) on a number line is given by AB = |b − a|. Side note: since distance cannot be negative, we use the absolute value.
entries.quote: The distance AB between two points A(a) and B(b)

entries.claim: If P is on segment AB such that AP:PB = m : n, P is said to divide AB internally in the ratio m : n.
entries.quote: point P is said to divide the line segment AB internally in the ratio

entries.claim: If Q is on the extension of segment AB such that AQ:QB = m : n, Q is said to divide AB externally in the ratio m : n.
entries.quote: point Q is said to divide the line segment AB externally in the ratio

entries.claim: (i) The coordinate of P dividing AB internally in the ratio m : n is P((na + mb)/(m + n)).
entries.quote: The coordinate of point P dividing segment AB internally in the ratio

entries.claim: (ii) The coordinate of Q dividing AB externally in the ratio m : n is Q((−na + mb)/(m − n)).
entries.quote: The coordinate of point Q dividing segment AB externally in the ratio

entries.claim: Side note beside formulas (i) and (ii): shows (na+mb)/(m+n) and (−na+mb)/(m−n); be careful with the order of multiplication (cross-multiply).
entries.quote: Be careful with the order of multiplication (cross-multiply).

entries.claim: The coordinate plane is divided into 4 quadrants as shown in the figure on the right, excluding the coordinate axes.
entries.quote: The coordinate plane is divided into 4 quadrants
entries.note: The claim is explicitly stated in the Point! box and illustrated in the coordinate plane figure on the right, showing the 4 quadrants with axes as boundaries (not part of the quadrants).

entries.claim: A point on the y-axis: the required point is (0, t).

entries.claim: A point on the line y = ax + b: the required point is (s, as+b).

entries.claim: Two points B, C are symmetric with respect to point A if and only if point A is the midpoint of segment BC.
entries.quote: Two points B, C are symmetric with respect to point A
entries.note: The rule is stated exactly on the page: 'Two points B, C are symmetric with respect to point A ⟺ Point A is the midpoint of segment BC.'

entries.claim: When finding symmetric points, first draw a diagram to understand the relative positions of the points. Next, let the required coordinates be (s, t) and express the midpoint in terms of s, t.
entries.quote: When finding symmetric points, first draw a diagram
entries.note: The method is stated exactly on the page in the Point! box, including all steps: first draw a diagram, then let coordinates be (s, t), then express the midpoint in terms of s, t.
